newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oilmin defers gasoline price rise.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oilmin defers gasoline price rise.

text.p: Venezuela's Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Wednesday he deferred a rise in domestic gasoline prices until July 31.
The rise had been due to take place on Thursday.
"For technical reasons, the change in (prices) in all service stations is not ready. The rise will take effect on July 31," he told journalists in the presidential Miraflores palace.
Prices in the domestic market are set by the Energy and Mines Ministry which has to keep them rising to keep pace with inflation, even though international prices have fallen over the past year.

The Ministry has proposed an average 27 percent rise across the various grades of fuel, but will soon relinquish it price- setting role if Congress approves a government proposal to liberalise the market.

Low 87 octane leaded gasoline is set to rise by 10 bolivars (2 cents) to 60 bolivars per litre, medium 91 octane leaded will rise 15 cents to 70 bolivars and high octane 95 leaded by 20 bolivars to 80 bolivars.
The move will bring prices up to about 90 percent of factory gate levels.
